reports.study: CT pancreas with IV contrast (pancreas protocol)
reports.text:
INDICATION: Pancreatic head mass on ultrasound, obstructive jaundice.
TECHNIQUE: Multiphase pancreas-protocol CT of the abdomen with IV contrast.
FINDINGS: 3.2 cm hypoattenuating mass in the pancreatic head. The mass encases the superior mesenteric artery for more than 180 degrees of its circumference. Common bile duct dilated to 14 mm and main pancreatic duct dilated to 6 mm upstream of the mass. Distended gallbladder without stones. No liver lesions. No ascites. Spleen, adrenal glands and kidneys normal. Bowel unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: 3.2 cm pancreatic head mass with SMA encasement greater than 180 degrees, compatible with locally advanced pancreatic cancer. No liver lesions or ascites.

reports.text:
INDICATION: Staging, pancreatic mass.
FINDINGS: Lungs clear without nodules. No pleural effusion. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary adenopathy. Heart normal in size.

events.reason: EUS with fine-needle aspiration and ERCP

procedures.procedure: Fine needle aspiration of lesion of pancreas using endoscopic ultrasonography guidance
ERCP with insertion of biliary metal stent

reports.text: Linear EUS: 3.1 cm hypoechoic, irregular mass in the pancreatic head. Dilated common bile duct and upstream pancreatic duct. No ascites. Fine-needle aspiration with a 22-gauge needle, 3 passes; on-site evaluation adequate.
reports.conclusion: 3.1 cm hypoechoic pancreatic head mass, sampled.

reports.text: Distal common bile duct stricture with upstream dilation. Biliary sphincterotomy. A fully covered self-expanding metal stent placed across the stricture with good drainage of bile and contrast.
reports.conclusion: Malignant-appearing distal bile duct stricture; covered metal biliary stent placed.

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: Pancreas, head mass, EUS-guided FNA with cell block.
DIAGNOSIS: Positive for malignancy. Adenocarcinoma with abundant extracellular and intracellular mucin (mucin-producing adenocarcinoma).

documents.title: EUS and ERCP report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology - advanced endoscopy
Date of procedure: 01/09/2026
Patient: Eugene Connolly, 71 M. Warfarin held since 1/4. Allergies: NKDA.
Indication: pancreatic head mass with obstructive jaundice.
EUS: 3.1 cm hypoechoic head mass; FNA x3.
ERCP: distal biliary stricture; sphincterotomy and fully covered metal stent placed with good drainage.
No immediate complications; discharged home the same day after recovery.
Cytology (final 1/12): mucin-producing adenocarcinoma.
Plan: resume warfarin 1/10 at usual dose. Referred to oncology - consult 1/14. Results discussed with the patient by phone today.

documents.title: Medical oncology consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside medical oncology practice
Date of visit: 01/14/2026
Re: Eugene Connolly, DOB 09/09/1954

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Connolly with a newly diagnosed pancreatic head adenocarcinoma.

History: three months of epigastric pain, poor appetite and weight loss, then jaundice. CA 19-9 150. CT 1/6: 3.2 cm head mass encasing the SMA beyond 180 degrees, no liver lesions, no ascites; chest CT clear. EUS-FNA 1/9: mucin-producing adenocarcinoma; covered metal biliary stent placed. Jaundice improving since the stent.
PMH: type 2 diabetes with neuropathy, hypertension, chronic AF on warfarin, past nodular BCC of the nose, pharyngoesophageal diverticulum (stapled 2022), right cataract surgery with endophthalmitis 2023, foot osteomyelitis 2024, appendectomy 12/2024. Normal coronary angiogram 2023.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, warfarin 5 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, capsaicin cream. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: paternal uncle with pancreatic cancer.
Performance status ECOG 1. Weight 77 kg.

Labs today: platelets 104, hemoglobin 11.6, fibrinogen 148 mg/dL, D-dimer 5.6 ug/mL FEU, INR 1.7 (warfarin restarted 1/10 after the procedure), total bilirubin 1.8.

Assessment:
1. Pancreatic adenocarcinoma, mucin-producing, head, locally advanced and unresectable (arterial encasement), no distant disease on imaging.
2. Chronic (compensated) disseminated intravascular coagulation related to the mucinous adenocarcinoma - low platelets and fibrinogen with raised D-dimer, no bleeding.
3. Chronic AF requiring anticoagulation.

Plan:
- Gemcitabine with nab-paclitaxel, days 1, 8 and 15 of 28-day cycles, starting 1/26.
- Anticoagulation: stop warfarin today; start enoxaparin 80 mg subcutaneously every 12 hours, which covers his AF and is preferred over warfarin with cancer-associated DIC. Teaching done in clinic.
- CA 19-9 and coagulation labs each cycle. Restaging CT after 2-3 cycles.
We will keep you updated. Please continue to manage his diabetes and blood pressure.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: First visit since his diagnosis. EUS 1/9 showed mucin-producing adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head, locally advanced (SMA encasement), no spread on CT; metal biliary stent placed, yellowing gone. Oncology found chronic DIC on labs and switched warfarin to enoxaparin 80 mg twice a day. Two doses of gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel so far - tired for a couple of days after each, mild nausea that the ondansetron handles. Appetite still poor, eating small meals. Pain much less since the stent.

Meds reconciled: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, HCTZ 12.5, atorvastatin 40, capsaicin cream, enoxaparin 80 mg SC q12h, ondansetron 4 mg ODT PRN; chemo at oncology. Warfarin stopped. NKDA.

O: Vitals as charted, weight 76 kg. Sclerae anicteric. Abdomen soft, nontender. Injection-site bruises on abdomen, small. Irregularly irregular, controlled. No edema.

A/P:
1. Pancreatic adenocarcinoma, locally advanced - under oncology. We talked about how he's coping; he is taking it a day at a time and wants to keep going with treatment.
2. Chronic DIC - oncology following labs each cycle.
3. AF - anticoagulated with enoxaparin; no INR checks needed now.
4. T2DM - eating less; sugars at home 110s-150s. Continue metformin, call for any reading under 80. BMP today.
5. HTN - BP fine, continue.
RTC 3 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Three cycles of gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel done. Restaging CT 4/13: pancreatic mass smaller, 2.7 cm, nothing new. CA 19-9 down to 96 in March. Fatigue is the main thing - naps most afternoons. Eating small meals several times a day. Nausea controlled. Enoxaparin twice daily, no bleeding. Home sugars 100s-140s, no lows.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, HCTZ 12.5, atorvastatin 40, capsaicin cream PRN, enoxaparin 80 mg SC q12h, ondansetron 4 mg ODT PRN; chemotherapy at oncology. NKDA.

O: Vitals as charted, weight 72 kg. Thin. Sclerae anicteric. Abdomen soft, nontender. Irregularly irregular. No edema. Feet intact.

A/P:
1. Pancreatic adenocarcinoma, locally advanced, responding on imaging - oncology managing.
2. Chronic DIC - improving per oncology labs.
3. T2DM: A1c 7.0, lower with weight loss and less intake. Continue metformin for now; check sugars daily, call for anything under 80. BMP today.
4. HTN: controlled, continue.
5. AF: on enoxaparin.
6. Advance care planning (about 20 minutes): talked through what matters most to him - staying at home and staying independent as long as he can. He wants full treatment for now. Gave him a health care proxy form and the state MOLST information to read; will review at next visit.
PHQ-2 1.
RTC early September, sooner as needed.
